decisions.reason: As a flagship cloud service central to the firm's stated direction and shown on the home page, it is likely above internal aspiration for strategic importance and will be retained while market feedback is still forming.

It extends the established document workflow offer and had its own page, so with recent launch uncertainty and available R&D slack the firm would likely keep it rather than redeploy resources immediately.
Although only mentioned on the website, it leverages existing messaging capabilities and serves legacy channel integration needs, making near-term withdrawal less likely than continued observation.

As a close-in optimization feature for fax delivery, it is not highly prominent but is inexpensive to sustain within the core platform, so boundedly rational management would usually keep it unless clear underperformance appears.

Threat protection fits the firm's security and compliance positioning well, and in a regulated B2B market management is likely to view it as strategically necessary even if early sales are still uncertain.

Multi-engine virus scanning complements the firm's secure messaging stack and likely shares resources with existing services, so the firm would tend to keep it while assessing whether it meets aspiration levels.
